hero.description: The US–Iran confrontation remains highly volatile as oil prices stay elevated and investors assess the risks to global energy supplies. featured.title: US–Iran Conflict Keeps Global Energy Markets on Edge
featured.content: The confrontation between the United States and Iran remains unresolved, with continued military tensions keeping investors concerned about energy supplies and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude has risen to around $95.67 a barrel and is heading for its strongest weekly gain since mid-July.

articles.title: BREAKING: US–Iran Tensions Continue
articles.description: The United States and Iran remain locked in a highly volatile confrontation following renewed military attacks. Washington has signalled that diplomacy remains difficult while Tehran continues to respond to US military operations.

articles.title: Oil Heads for Strongest Weekly Gain Since July
articles.description: Brent crude rose to around $95.67 a barrel early Friday, putting it on course for a weekly gain of about 7.1%. US West Texas Intermediate reached about $91.56 and is up almost 10% for the week.

articles.title: Hormuz Shipping Disruption Remains a Major Concern
articles.description: The continuing US–Iran confrontation is creating uncertainty around commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Any prolonged disruption could place additional pressure on global energy supplies and prices.

articles.title: Nepal Flood Losses Estimated at $2.56 Billion
articles.description: Nepal's catastrophic August flooding has caused an estimated 387.5 billion Nepalese rupees, or about $2.56 billion, in economic losses. Authorities say more than 1,250 people have died and more than 4,200 remain missing.

articles.title: Engineers Help Guide Nepal Rescue Operation
articles.description: More than 500 engineers have been using a WhatsApp group to share tunnel layouts and structural information with rescue teams searching for people believed to be trapped at hydropower facilities.

morningSummary.title: MORNING SUMMARY
morningSummary.description: The global picture this Friday is dominated by geopolitical tension, energy prices, extreme weather and monetary policy. The US–Iran confrontation remains unresolved and is keeping Brent crude above $95 a barrel, with oil heading for its strongest weekly gain since July. Nepal continues to recover from catastrophic flooding that has killed more than 1,250 people and left more than 4,200 missing, while estimated economic losses have reached about $2.56 billion. China is dealing with severe flooding from Typhoon Saudel, with tens of thousands evacuated. Asian markets have rebounded ahead of important US employment data, while the Japanese yen has strengthened as expectations of a Bank of Japan rate hike increase.
